userStories.title: nax-agent: a loop-handler role option
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the native facade's optional loop-handler role without changing existing callers.

**Motivation** — The session must know the repo's rules.

**Approach** — **Loop-handler role (US-001).** `NativeBackendOptions` gains `loopHandlerRole?: string`. When set, `openNative` adds `role` to the `loopHandlerContext` it builds; when unset the context has no `role` key. `parseNativeBackendOptions` accepts it as a non-empty string. `"tui"` is a loop-handler and cost-ledger role only; it is not added to `KNOWN_SESSION_ROLES` (`src/runtime/session-role.ts`), because chat never dispatches through `SessionManager`.

`openNative` — Baseline:
```typescript
const loopHandlerContext = { sessionName: ctx.sessionId, workdir: ctx.workdir, model: raw.model, provider: resolved.provider };
```
Target: the same object plus `role: raw.loopHandlerRole` when `raw.loopHandlerRole !== undefined`.

**Scope** — In: update native-backend-options.ts and native-backend.ts and add the role regression cases. Out: chat opener and rule-role allowlists belong to US-006 and US-005; no workflow role-registry extension. The API snapshot lists exported names only (NativeBackendOptions appears as one type line), so a new optional field changes no existing assertion.

**Interface** — Target adds to `NativeBackendOptions`:
```typescript
/** Copied into every turn's loop-handler context as `role` (for example "tui"). */
readonly loopHandlerRole?: string;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Opening a session through nativeBackend({ model, loopHandlerRole: "tui" }) yields turn options whose loopHandlerContext.role is "tui".
[unit] Opening a session through nativeBackend({ model }) with no loopHandlerRole yields a loopHandlerContext with no role key.
[unit] nativeBackend({ model, loopHandlerRole: "" }) throws AgentSessionError with code AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS.

routing.reasoning: Small additive backend/type change, but the session role controls rule delivery and requires security-isolated TDD.

userStories.title: The chat prompt builder
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add pure chat instruction and feature-message builders under the Prompt Builder Convention.

**Motivation** — One agent for the whole loop.

**Approach** — **Prompt (US-004).** New `packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/chat-builder.ts` (Prompt Builder Convention), exported from `src/prompts`:
- `buildChatInstructions({ mode, rulesIndex })` -> the system prompt: one intro paragraph (an interactive coding agent working in this repository with the person), a `## Permission mode` section (full: tools run without asking; guarded: edits, deletes, commits and every shell command are put to the person), a `## Commands outside the sandbox` section (set `unsandboxed: true` with an `unsandboxedReason` only when a command needs the network, the Docker socket, a local port or a device the sandbox blocks), and `buildRulesIndexSection({ entries: rulesIndex, shownAutomatically: true })`.
- `buildChatFeatureMessage({ feature, spec, prd?, message })` -> the user message `/feature` sends: a `## Feature <name>` block with the spec text and, when `prd` is given, the PRD JSON, each in a fenced block, then the person's message (which may be empty).

**Scope** — In: new builder, pure output assertions and exports from src/prompts/index.ts. Out: loading rules and opening sessions is US-006; reading feature files and dispatching slash commands is US-014. The design's nax context fragments repo summary is not added; repository instructions already come from AGENTS.md.

**Interface** —
```typescript
buildChatInstructions({ mode, rulesIndex })
buildChatFeatureMessage({ feature, spec, prd?, message })
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] buildChatInstructions imported from src/prompts is a function.
[unit] buildChatInstructions({ mode: "guarded", rulesIndex: [] }) contains ## Permission mode.
[unit] buildChatInstructions({ mode: "guarded", rulesIndex: [] }) returns text stating that every shell command is put to the person before it runs.
[unit] buildChatInstructions({ mode: "full", rulesIndex: [] }) states that tools run without asking.

[unit] Given one rulesIndex entry, buildChatInstructions returns a rules section saying each rule's full text is shown the first time a file it applies to is read, written or edited.
[unit] With rulesIndex: [], buildChatInstructions returns a prompt with no ## Rules index section.
[unit] buildChatFeatureMessage({ feature: "auth", spec: "S", prd: "{}", message: "go" }) starts with ## Feature auth.
[unit] buildChatFeatureMessage({ feature: "auth", spec: "S", prd: "{}", message: "go" }) returns the spec text S and the PRD text {} before the person's message go, which ends the message.
[unit] buildChatFeatureMessage({ feature: "auth", spec: "S", message: "go" }) with no prd has exactly one fenced block.

routing.reasoning: Pure prompt formatting and existing-builder composition; no permission enforcement or lifecycle state.

userStories.title: Chat modes and the tui rule role
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Define chat's two permission mappings and enable existing on-demand rule delivery for tui.

**Motivation** — The session must know the repo's rules.

**Approach** — **Modes and the `tui` rule role (US-005).** `packages/nax/src/chat/chat-mode.ts`:

| `ChatMode` | `profile` | `bashApproval` | `SessionMeta.mode` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `full` | `full` | `raw` | `full` |
| `guarded` (default) | `ask` | `gated` | `ask` |

`nextChatMode("guarded")` is `"full"` and `nextChatMode("full")` is `"guarded"`. `chatModeOfMeta(meta.mode)` maps `ask` to `guarded`, `full` to `full`, and `none` or `read` (sessions koda created) to `null`: such a session is refused, never widened. `RULE_READ_ROLES` and `RULE_WRITE_ROLES` gain `"tui"`.

**Scope** — In: chat-mode.ts, initial chat/index.ts exports and adding tui to both rule lists; verify first-Write refusal and Read nudge through the existing handlers. Out: backend role propagation is US-001; session lock/open logic is US-006. `"tui"` is not added to KNOWN_SESSION_ROLES or the session role registry; chat never dispatches through SessionManager.

**Interface** — Export from src/chat/index.ts:
```typescript
export type ChatMode = "full" | "guarded";
export interface ChatSessionSettings { readonly profile: "full" | "ask"; readonly bashApproval: "raw" | "gated"; readonly metaMode: "full" | "ask" }
export function chatSessionSettings(mode: ChatMode): ChatSessionSettings;
export function nextChatMode(mode: ChatMode): ChatMode;
export function chatModeOfMeta(mode: SessionMeta["mode"]): ChatMode | null;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] chatSessionSettings("full") returns { profile: "full", bashApproval: "raw", metaMode: "full" }.
[unit] chatSessionSettings("guarded") returns { profile: "ask", bashApproval: "gated", metaMode: "ask" }.
[unit] nextChatMode("guarded") returns "full".
[unit] nextChatMode("full") returns "guarded".
[unit] chatModeOfMeta("ask") returns "guarded".
[unit] chatModeOfMeta("full") returns "full".
[unit] chatModeOfMeta("read") returns null.
[unit] chatModeOfMeta("none") returns null.
[unit] RULE_READ_ROLES contains "tui".
[unit] createRuleDeliveryHandlers with role tui in the loop context refuses a first Write to a file a rule covers, as it does for wf-implementer.
[unit] With role tui, a Read of a file a rule covers is nudged with that rule's text.

routing.reasoning: Straightforward mappings and role additions, but access-control modes and role checks require security-isolated TDD.

userStories.title: The chat session opener
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Open or resume a locked shared-store native chat session with mode-specific settings and repository rules.

**Motivation** — koda must see the same sessions.

**Approach** — **Opening a session (US-006).** `openChatSession(request, deps)` in `packages/nax/src/chat/open-chat-session.ts`. The request carries `storage`, `cwd`, `repoRoot`, `mode?`, `model?` (required for a new session, optional on a resume), `resumeId?`, `loopHandlers`, and `config` (the loaded `NaxConfig`). The same module exports `resolveChatSessionsDir(env)` (`env.NAX_AGENT_SESSIONS_DIR` when set, else `defaultSessionsDir(globalConfigDir())`) and `createChatStorage({ env, pid, now, logger })`, which returns `createSessionStorage({ dir: resolveChatSessionsDir(env), pid, now, logger })`; `chatCommand` builds the one storage the host and every open share. In order:
1. Transcripts = `createFileTranscriptStore(storage.dir)`; `now` comes from `_openChatSessionDeps.now`.
2. New session: id = `randomUUID()`, `acquireLock(id)`, then `writeMeta({ schemaVersion: 1, sessionId, cwd, mode, model, bashApproval, title: null, createdAt: now, updatedAt: null })`. Resume: `readMeta(id)` (null refuses `CHAT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND`; `SESSION_META_UNREADABLE` propagates), `chatModeOfMeta` (null refuses `CHAT_SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED`), then `acquireLock(id)`. The request's `mode` and `model` override the stored ones only when the caller passes them (a switch); a plain resume uses the stored mode and model.
3. Rules index: `resolveRuleSet({ repoRoot, packageDir: repoRoot, overrideDir, overrideMode })` (from `config.context.rules`) mapped with `toRulesIndexEntry`; instructions = `buildChatInstructions({ mode, rulesIndex })`. The index lists repo-level rules; package-scoped rules are still delivered on demand by the handlers.
4. Backend = `nativeBackend({ model, bashApproval, allowUnsandboxed: true, allowUnsandboxedCommands: true, carryHistoryAcrossModels: true, loopHandlers: request.loopHandlers, loopHandlerRole: "tui", catalogOverrides?, compaction? })`, where `catalogOverrides` is `config.agent.native.catalogOverrides` when non-empty and `compaction` is `config.execution.compaction` when set. Both modes set `allowUnsandboxed: true` (full runs unsandboxed when the sandbox is unavailable; guarded asks before every Bash command, so an unwrapped command is still asked) and `allowUnsandboxedCommands: true` (F1's per-command escalation).
5. `transcripts.load(id)`: null -> `createAgentSession`, else `resumeAgentSession(id, options)`, with `{ backend, sessionId, profile, workdir: cwd, instructions, transcriptStore, approvalTimeoutMs: config.execution.approvalTimeout }`.
6. If any step after `acquireLock` throws, the lock is released and the error rethrown.
Returns `ChatSessionHandle = { session, meta, release }`. The instructions describe the mode only; the sandbox state (`session.backend.sandbox`) is shown by the shell.

Create `_openChatSessionDeps` for createAgentSession, resumeAgentSession, nativeBackend, createSessionStorage, createFileTranscriptStore, resolveRuleSet, randomUUID, env and now. Missing metadata throws `NaxError` code `CHAT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, message `no session <id> in <dir>`; unsupported stored mode throws `CHAT_SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED`, message `session <id> was created in mode <mode>; nax chat opens full or ask sessions only`. Both refuse before taking a lock, as does corrupt metadata.

All ACs drive `openChatSession` through `_openChatSessionDeps` fakes; the request's `storage` is a real `createSessionStorage` over a temp directory. Persist `chatSessionSettings(mode).metaMode`, not the UI name guarded, in SessionMeta.mode. SessionMeta timestamps are persisted as ISO strings; preserve the storage factory's now() -> Date contract.

**Scope** — In: opener, storage-directory factory, dependency seam and exports through src/chat/index.ts. Out: latest-session selection, locked-session error translation and transactional host switches are US-010/011; Ink rendering is US-012. Sessions directory uses only NAX_AGENT_SESSIONS_DIR/global config dir, not ACP --sessions-dir or agentServer.sessionsDir. No durable chat tool-call audit directory and no RunCommand offering change.

**Interface** —
```typescript
export interface ChatSessionHandle { readonly session: AgentSession; readonly meta: SessionMeta; readonly release: () => Promise<void> }
openChatSession(request, deps)
resolveChatSessionsDir(env)
createChatStorage({ env, pid, now, logger })
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Opening a new guarded session passes nativeBackend bashApproval: "gated".
[unit] Opening a new guarded session passes nativeBackend allowUnsandboxed: true.
[unit] Opening a new guarded session passes nativeBackend allowUnsandboxedCommands: true.
[unit] Opening a new guarded session passes nativeBackend loopHandlerRole: "tui".
[unit] With agent.native.catalogOverrides holding one entry, nativeBackend receives catalogOverrides with that entry.
[unit] With execution.compaction.enabled: false, nativeBackend receives compaction.enabled false.
[unit] Opening a new full session passes createAgentSession profile: "full".
[unit] Opening a new full session passes createAgentSession workdir equal to the request's cwd.
[unit] Opening a new full session passes createAgentSession approvalTimeoutMs equal to execution.approvalTimeout.
[unit] With a repo whose .nax/rules/ holds one rule error-handling, the instructions passed to createAgentSession contain `error-handling`.
[unit] A new session writes metadata whose sessionId is the injected randomUUID value.
[unit] A new session holds the lock: storage.readLockHolder(id) returns state "own".
[unit] Resuming an id whose transcript store has a document calls resumeAgentSession with that id and never createAgentSession.
[unit] Resuming an id with metadata but no transcript document calls createAgentSession with that sessionId.
[unit] Resuming with no mode or model in the request opens with the stored mode and model.
[unit] Resuming an id with no metadata rejects with NaxError code CHAT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND.
[unit] Resuming an id whose metadata mode is read rejects with code CHAT_SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED.
[unit] Resuming an id whose metadata file holds invalid JSON rejects with code SESSION_META_UNREADABLE.
[unit] When createAgentSession throws after the lock was taken, openChatSession rejects with that error and readLockHolder(id) returns null.
[unit] resolveChatSessionsDir({ NAX_AGENT_SESSIONS_DIR: "/tmp/s" }) returns /tmp/s.
[unit] resolveChatSessionsDir({}) returns defaultSessionsDir(globalConfigDir()).
[unit] When resume metadata is missing, openChatSession rejects with message no session <id> in <dir> without acquiring the session lock.

[unit] When stored metadata mode is none or read, openChatSession rejects with message session <id> was created in mode <mode>; nax chat opens full or ask sessions only without acquiring the session lock.
[unit] When resume metadata is corrupt, openChatSession propagates SESSION_META_UNREADABLE without acquiring the session lock.

routing.reasoning: Integrates durable metadata/locks, transcript resume, backend policy and rules; security-sensitive session ownership requires strict TDD.

userStories.title: The ask controller
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Centralize terminal approval/question state and safe per-session positive approval memory.

**Motivation** — "Always allow" must not fork.

**Approach** — **Asks (US-007).** `createChatAskController({ mode, answer })` in `packages/nax/src/chat/ask-controller.ts`; `answer` is a function the host points at the current session (it follows the session across a switch). Events:
- `approval_requested` with `answerable: false`: ignored (never answered, never pending).
- full mode: `answer(requestId, { decision: "allow" })` at once.
- guarded mode: a remembered `allow` stored under `approvalMemoryKey(event)` answers at once when `approvalMemoryApplies(event, "allow")` holds and the event is not `unsandboxed`; otherwise the ask joins `pending()`. The person resolves it with `resolve(requestId, "allow_once" | "allow_session" | "deny")`. `allow_session` stores `allow` under the key only when `canRemember(event)`: the key is defined, the event is not `unsandboxed`, and the tool is not `Delete`; otherwise it answers allow once. `deny` is never remembered.
- `question` with `answerable !== false` joins `pending()` in both modes and is resolved with `answerQuestion(requestId, text)`.
- `approval_resolved` removes its request from `pending()`.
- `setMode(mode)` changes the mode for later events; `reset()` clears the memory and `pending()`. The host keeps the memory across a mode or model switch (same session) and calls `reset()` on `/clear` and on a resume of another session.
- `onChange(listener)` notifies the shell and the fallback.

Export it from src/chat/index.ts. The shared helpers must be consumed, not copied: a remembered allow for Bash npm test answers npm test but not npm test; rm -rf x.

**Scope** — In: controller state/events, safe memory, answer/question dispatch and subscriptions. Out: delayed interaction-chain timers are US-008; session binding/reset during host replacement is US-010/011; rendering/key selection is US-013.

**Interface** —
```typescript
export type AskChoice = "allow_once" | "allow_session" | "deny";
createChatAskController({ mode, answer })
```
The controller exposes handle, pending, resolve, canRemember, answerQuestion, setMode, reset and onChange as described above.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] In full mode, an approval_requested event r1 calls answer("r1", { decision: "allow" }) once.
[unit] In full mode, an approval_requested event with answerable: false calls no answer.
[unit] In guarded mode, an approval_requested event joins pending() and calls no answer.
[unit] resolve("r1", "allow_once") calls answer("r1", { decision: "allow" }).
[unit] resolve("r1", "deny") calls answer("r1", { decision: "deny" }).
[unit] After resolve("r1", "allow_session") for tool Bash command npm test, a later request for npm test is answered allow without joining pending().
[unit] After resolve("r1", "allow_session") for Bash npm test, a later request for npm test; rm -rf x joins pending().
[unit] After resolve("r1", "allow_session") for Bash npm test, a later request for npm test with unsandboxed: true joins pending().
[unit] After resolve("r1", "deny") for npm test, a later request for npm test joins pending().
[unit] canRemember returns false for a request whose command is rm -f x.
[unit] canRemember returns false for a request with unsandboxed: true.
[unit] canRemember returns false for a request whose tool is Delete.
[unit] resolve("r1", "allow_session") on a request that cannot be remembered answers allow and stores nothing: a later identical request joins pending().
[unit] An approval_resolved event for r1 removes r1 from pending() without calling answer.
[unit] In full mode, a question event q1 joins pending().
[unit] answerQuestion("q1", "yes") calls answer("q1", { text: "yes" }) and removes q1 from pending().
[unit] After setMode("full"), a new approval_requested event is answered allow at once.
[unit] After reset(), a request remembered before is put in pending() again.
[unit] Each change to pending() calls every onChange listener once.

routing.reasoning: New stateful approval/question controller with security-critical memory restrictions and answer arbitration.

suggestedCriteria: When resolve is called twice for the same pending request, answer is called only for the first resolution.
When a question event has answerable:false, pending() is unchanged and answer is not called.

userStories.title: Offer unanswered asks to the interaction chain
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Offer pending terminal approvals to the configured interaction chain after a configurable delay without double answering.

**Motivation** — One agent for the whole loop.

**Approach** — **Interaction-chain fallback (US-008).** `createAskFallback({ controller, chain, delayMs, logger })` in `packages/nax/src/chat/ask-fallback.ts`, timers through `_askFallbackDeps.setTimeout` / `clearTimeout` (the `setTimeout` exception in `forbidden-patterns-source.md` applies: each handle is cleared when its ask leaves `pending()`; say so at the call site). For each pending approval (not questions) a timer of `delayMs` starts when it joins `pending()`. On expiry, when `chain` is non-null, it calls `chain.prompt(request)` with `{ id: "chat-<requestId>", type: "confirm", featureName: "chat", stage: "custom", summary, detail: "<command>\n<reason>", fallback: "skip", createdAt }`, where `command` is the event's `command` as the session sent it (already masked) and is omitted when absent. Response mapping, applied only while the ask is still in `pending()`: `approve` -> `allow_once`; `reject` or `abort` -> `deny`; any other action (`skip`, which a chain timeout or `cancel()` produces, `choose`, `input`) is ignored and the ask stays in the TUI. A response for an ask no longer in `pending()` is ignored. If the ask leaves `pending()` first, its timer is cleared, or, when the chain prompt is already out, `chain.cancel("chat-<requestId>")` is called once. A rejected `chain.prompt` logs warn `chat ask fallback failed` with `errorMessage(err)` only, and the ask stays in the TUI. `dispose()` clears every timer. `delayMs` is new config `interaction.defaults.chatAskFallbackMs` (int, 1000 to 3600000, default 60000).

`InteractionConfigSchema.defaults` in src/config/schemas-infra.ts adds `chatAskFallbackMs: z.number().int().min(1000).max(3600000).default(60000)`; the literal interaction default object in src/config/schemas.ts gains `chatAskFallbackMs: 60000` beside timeout; the hand-written InteractionConfig type in src/config/runtime-types.ts gains optional `chatAskFallbackMs?: number` in defaults (optional so existing InteractionConfig fixtures still typecheck), and the host uses 60000 when absent; FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS in src/cli/config-descriptions.ts gains interaction.defaults.chatAskFallbackMs. Keep defaults.fallback undefined unless configured. No configured chain, or the headless CLI plugin, means no fallback; terminal asks wait until the session's own approval timeout.

All ACs inject `_askFallbackDeps` timers driven by the shared fake clock helper, and a fake chain.

**Scope** — In: fallback lifecycle/timers, chain mapping, dependency seam and all four config surfaces, including preserving the existing undefined defaults.fallback when no override is configured. Out: chain construction/startup degradation is US-015; controller decisions are US-007; host composition is US-010. Questions are not offered to the interaction chain; only approvals are.

**Interface** —
```typescript
createAskFallback({ controller, chain, delayMs, logger })
```
Returned fallback exposes dispose().
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] A guarded ask pending for less than delayMs has not prompted the chain.
[unit] Once delayMs passes, the chain's prompt is called once with id chat-r1.
[unit] When delayMs expires for a pending approval, chain.prompt receives a request with type confirm, stage custom, featureName chat and fallback skip.
[unit] When delayMs expires for a pending approval with a command, chain.prompt receives detail containing that command as sent by the session and the approval's reason.
[unit] A chain response with action: "approve" resolves the ask allow_once.
[unit] A chain response with action: "reject" resolves the ask deny.
[unit] A chain response with action: "skip" leaves the ask in pending().
[unit] A chain response that arrives after the ask left pending() resolves nothing.
[unit] When the ask is resolved in the TUI before delayMs, the chain is never prompted.
[unit] When the ask is resolved in the TUI after the prompt went out, chain.cancel("chat-r1") is called once.
[unit] When an approval_resolved event removes the ask after the prompt went out, chain.cancel("chat-r1") is called once.
[unit] A rejected chain.prompt logs warn chat ask fallback failed with errorMessage(err) only and the ask stays in pending().
[unit] With chain null, no prompt is made and the ask stays in pending().
[unit] A pending question is never offered to the chain.
[unit] dispose() clears pending timers: advancing the clock past delayMs afterwards prompts nothing.
[unit] Parsing an empty config yields interaction.defaults.chatAskFallbackMs equal to 60000.
[unit] Parsing a config with interaction.defaults.chatAskFallbackMs: 500 fails validation.
[unit] FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS["interaction.defaults.chatAskFallbackMs"] is a non-empty string.
[unit] With no interaction chain, an unanswered approval remains pending until the session's approval timeout resolves it; fallback sends no answer.
[unit] Parsing an empty config after adding chatAskFallbackMs leaves interaction.defaults.fallback undefined, preserving the existing per-trigger fallback behavior.

routing.reasoning: Concurrent timer/remote/TUI permission decisions with cancellation and late replies form a security-critical first-answer-wins path.

suggestedCriteria: When the chain responds abort for a still-pending approval, the controller resolves it deny.
When the chain responds choose or input for a still-pending approval, the approval remains pending and no answer is sent.
When a rejected chain.prompt contains an Error with message bad token, the warning's error value is bad token rather than the error object or stack.

userStories.title: Turns, the chat cost ledger and metadata updates
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Run chat turns through the controller and durable cost ledger, then update shared session metadata.

**Motivation** — koda must see the same sessions.

**Approach** — **Turns and cost (US-009).** `runChatTurn({ handle, storage, message, asks, ledger, onEvent, now })` in `packages/nax/src/chat/turn-runner.ts` iterates `session.send(message)`, passes `approval_requested`, `approval_resolved` and `question` events to `asks.handle`, every `usage` event to `ledger.record`, and every event to `onEvent`. **Goal** — Render the interactive chat transcript, multi-line input, status and notices independently of the run TUI.

**Motivation** — Today nax has no interactive front door: every native session is a nax run story or the ACP server behind koda.

**Approach** — **Shell (US-012, US-013, US-014).** `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/`, rendered with ink `render(..., { exitOnCtrlC: false })`:
- `ChatApp.tsx` (root), `Transcript.tsx`: assistant text streamed from `text_delta`; one line per `tool_call`, `<tool> <detail>` where detail is `input.path` for Read, Write, Edit and Delete, `input.command` for Bash, and nothing otherwise, cut to 60 characters, marked `ok` or `error` by its `tool_result`; `thinking_delta` collapsed to one `thinking...` line.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Register chat as the explicit/default CLI front door and compose config, shared storage, interaction chain and shell safely.

**Motivation** — Today nax has no interactive front door: every native session is a nax run story or the ACP server behind koda.

**Approach** — **CLI entry (US-015).** `registerChatCommand(program, deps)` in `packages/nax/src/cli/chat.ts` registers `program.command("chat", { isDefault: true })` with `--resume [id]`, `--mode <full|guarded>`, `--model <id>`, `--profile <name>` (repeatable; a collector defined in `chat.ts`, since `collectProfile` in `bin/nax.ts` is not importable) and `-d, --dir <path>`; its action calls `chatCommand(options, deps)`. `bin/nax.ts` only calls `registerChatCommand`.
`chatCommand`: refuses when stdin is not a TTY; validates `--mode`; finds the project with `findProjectDir(dir)` (`repoRoot` = its parent, or `dir` when there is none); loads config with `loadConfig(naxDir, { profile })` when `profile` is non-empty; resolves the model (`--model`, else `models.native.balanced`, read as for `host.models`); builds the storage with `createChatStorage`; builds the chain with `initInteractionChain(config, true)` (headless, so a `cli` plugin yields null), and on a throw writes `interaction chain unavailable: <message>; asks stay in the terminal` to stderr and continues with no chain; builds the host with `createChatHost`, starts or resumes, registers `SIGTERM` and `SIGHUP` handlers (through `deps.onSignal`) that call `host.close()`, then calls `renderChat`. An unknown first argument (`nax rnu`) is an excess argument to the default command (commander 13 rejects excess arguments by default) and never opens a session.

Create `_chatCommandDeps` (stdinIsTTY, loadConfig, findProjectDir, initInteractionChain, createChatHost, renderChat, onSignal, writeErr, setExitCode). Non-TTY writes `nax chat needs an interactive terminal`, sets exit code 1 and opens no session. Invalid mode writes `unknown mode <value>; expected full or guarded`, exit 1. A locked-session resume writes its exact message and never renders. SIGTERM/SIGHUP close releases the lock before exit. A plain resume passes no launch-default settings that would overwrite its stored mode/model; explicit settings may be applied through the host's existing switch surface. Keep signal references removable and close resources on startup failure.

**Scope** — In: CLI module, one bin registration, startup/error/signal wiring and commander/smoke assertions, including proving existing explicit status dispatch is not intercepted by the new default command. ```typescript

```typescript
chatCommand(options, deps)
```
